page: Microsoft Azure NC36lds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supplies 36 dedicated vCPUs alongside 72.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a compute-heavy memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features a bundled 1993 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by Premium Storage capability for external storage volumes.

Hardware acceleration is provisioned via a fractional 0.25 partition of an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU from the Blackwell family. This fractional GPU slice provides 24 GB of total VRAM, enabling hardware-accelerated processing without dedicating a full physical GPU module. Networking provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating existing network infrastructure configurations such as virtual networks or gateways for external connectivity.

The instance exhibits a balance between extensive thread concurrency and localized graphic processing. With 36 dedicated cores paired with an entry-level GPU fraction, the configuration targets compute-dense workloads that require modest GPU acceleration rather than full accelerator allocation. Cost efficiency is achieved by partitioning modern Blackwell-generation GPU hardware into a quarter-slice, avoiding the resource overhead and operational expense of an unpartitioned flagship card.

Workload fit covers batch visualization pipelines, workstation-level rendering, lightweight machine learning inference, and multi-threaded engineering simulations that leverage local high-speed NVMe storage caches alongside partitioned GPU compute.
